feed.title: Ebola Tracker: DR Congo
feed.subtitle: Independent, sourced tracker of the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in DR Congo: confirmed cases and deaths, affected provinces, spread to other countries, vaccines, WHO risk and a dated timeline.

entry.title: Kenya confirms a third Ebola case
entry.summary: Kenya's health ministry said a close contact of the first two patients, who had been in quarantine since 6 October, tested positive. The ministry said there was no evidence of community spread, and contacts continue daily monitoring for 21 days. Kenya now has three confirmed cases and one death.
entry.content:
Kenya's health ministry said a close contact of the first two patients, who had been in quarantine since 6 October, tested positive. The ministry said there was no evidence of community spread, and contacts continue daily monitoring for 21 days. Kenya now has three confirmed cases and one death.

Sources: WHO Africa, The Washington Post, Al Jazeera

entry.title: Media report Ebola in an eighth province, North Ubangi
entry.summary: Reuters and Bloomberg report, citing health officials, two confirmed Ebola cases in North Ubangi province, which borders the Central African Republic. Reuters says Congolese authorities had not yet officially announced the cases. It also reports that several suspected Ebola deaths had recently occurred at a mining site in Wapinda health zone, with samples sent for laboratory analysis in the province and in Kinshasa.
entry.content:
Reuters and Bloomberg report, citing health officials, two confirmed Ebola cases in North Ubangi province, which borders the Central African Republic. It also reports that several suspected Ebola deaths had recently occurred at a mining site in Wapinda health zone, with samples sent for laboratory analysis in the province and in Kinshasa.

Sources: Reuters via TimesLIVE, Bloomberg

entry.title: ECDC: 9,277 cases and 4,478 deaths
entry.summary: ECDC reports 9,277 confirmed cases and 4,478 deaths in DR Congo as of 15 October (data to 14 October), with 924 patients in isolation in hospital. New cases in the latest report were in Ituri (31), North Kivu (28), Haut-Uele (5) and Tshopo (1). ECDC also notes the media reports of cases in North Ubangi.
entry.content:
ECDC reports 9,277 confirmed cases and 4,478 deaths in DR Congo as of 15 October (data to 14 October), with 924 patients in isolation in hospital. New cases in the latest report were in Ituri (31), North Kivu (28), Haut-Uele (5) and Tshopo (1). ECDC also notes the media reports of cases in North Ubangi.

Sources: ECDC

entry.title: Kenya confirms a second Ebola case
entry.summary: Kenya's health ministry said a relative of the first patient, who was already in quarantine and under daily monitoring, tested positive after developing symptoms on 13 October. The ministry said it identified 128 contacts of the first patient and found no evidence of spread in the community. Kenya now has two confirmed cases and one death.
entry.content:
Kenya's health ministry said a relative of the first patient, who was already in quarantine and under daily monitoring, tested positive after developing symptoms on 13 October. The ministry said it identified 128 contacts of the first patient and found no evidence of spread in the community. Kenya now has two confirmed cases and one death.

Sources: AP via WRAL, CBC, The Washington Post

entry.title: ECDC and CDC: 9,144 cases and 4,410 deaths
entry.summary: ECDC reports 9,144 confirmed cases and 4,410 deaths in DR Congo as of 13 October (data to 12 October), with 899 patients in isolation in hospital and 65 of 167 health zones affected across 7 provinces. CDC's situation summary of 14 October lists the same DR Congo totals and 2 confirmed cases and 1 death in Kenya.
entry.content:
ECDC reports 9,144 confirmed cases and 4,410 deaths in DR Congo as of 13 October (data to 12 October), with 899 patients in isolation in hospital and 65 of 167 health zones affected across 7 provinces. CDC's situation summary of 14 October lists the same DR Congo totals and 2 confirmed cases and 1 death in Kenya.

Sources: ECDC, CDC: current situation

entry.title: DR Congo reports 9,066 cases and 4,381 deaths
entry.summary: DR Congo's health ministry reported 9,066 confirmed Ebola cases and 4,381 deaths in its update of 13 October, according to Al Jazeera and Xinhua. Media reports describe it as the country's largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak. Ituri province accounts for most confirmed cases.
entry.content:
DR Congo's health ministry reported 9,066 confirmed Ebola cases and 4,381 deaths in its update of 13 October, according to Al Jazeera and Xinhua. Media reports describe it as the country's largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak. Ituri province accounts for most confirmed cases.

Sources: Al Jazeera, Xinhua

entry.title: WHO experts: Tumaini vaccine trial expected by end of October
entry.summary: WHO experts said the Tumaini trial in DR Congo is expected to begin by the end of October. It will first test Ervebo, which is licensed for the Zaire strain, to see whether it protects against Bundibugyo virus. Candidates from Oxford and Moderna, now in early-phase trials, may be added later. Whether Ervebo protects against this strain is not yet known.
entry.content:

Sources: AFP via Medical Xpress, CEPI

entry.title: ECDC: 8,728 cases and 4,205 deaths
entry.summary: ECDC's update of 7 October, with data to 6 October, reports DR Congo's confirmed total at 8,728 cases, including 4,205 deaths. Ituri has 6,513 cases and North Kivu 1,785. ECDC notes that DR Congo's figures are under continuous review and may be revised.
entry.content:
ECDC's update of 7 October, with data to 6 October, reports DR Congo's confirmed total at 8,728 cases, including 4,205 deaths. Ituri has 6,513 cases and North Kivu 1,785. ECDC notes that DR Congo's figures are under continuous review and may be revised.

Sources: ECDC

entry.title: CDC: 8,787 cases and 4,242 deaths
entry.summary: CDC's situation summary counts 8,787 confirmed cases and 4,242 confirmed deaths in DR Congo as of 7 October. DR Congo's health ministry does not include probable cases in its official reporting.
entry.content:
CDC's situation summary counts 8,787 confirmed cases and 4,242 confirmed deaths in DR Congo as of 7 October. DR Congo's health ministry does not include probable cases in its official reporting.

Sources: CDC: current situation, PM News

entry.title: Bundibugyo vaccine trial begins in Uganda
entry.summary: The MRC/UVRI & LSHTM Uganda Research Unit vaccinated the first participants in Masaka City with a candidate vaccine developed by the University of Oxford. The early-phase study tests safety and immune response in healthy adults and follows a trial of the same candidate in the UK. It does not yet show whether the vaccine protects against the virus.
entry.content:
The MRC/UVRI & LSHTM Uganda Research Unit vaccinated the first participants in Masaka City with a candidate vaccine developed by the University of Oxford. The early-phase study tests safety and immune response in healthy adults and follows a trial of the same candidate in the UK. It does not yet show whether the vaccine protects against the virus.

Sources: MRC/UVRI & LSHTM Uganda Research Unit, Xinhua, The Independent (Uganda)

entry.title: Kenya's first imported case dies in Nairobi
entry.summary: A Kenyan citizen living in DR Congo travelled by road to Kampala and flew to Nairobi on 3 October. He tested positive and died on 5 October. Contacts are being followed.
entry.content:
A Kenyan citizen living in DR Congo travelled by road to Kampala and flew to Nairobi on 3 October. He tested positive and died on 5 October. Contacts are being followed.

Sources: WHO Africa, Citizen Digital, Al Jazeera

entry.title: CDC and ECDC: 8,603 cases and 4,148 deaths
entry.summary: DR Congo's confirmed total reaches 8,603 cases, including 4,148 deaths, with data to 4 October. ECDC notes that DR Congo's figures are under continuous review and may be revised.
entry.content:
DR Congo's confirmed total reaches 8,603 cases, including 4,148 deaths, with data to 4 October. ECDC notes that DR Congo's figures are under continuous review and may be revised.

Sources: CDC: current situation, ECDC

entry.title: CDC: 8,442 cases and 4,080 deaths
entry.summary: CDC calls it the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record and says it is spreading faster than earlier ones. No cases in the US.
entry.content:
CDC calls it the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record and says it is spreading faster than earlier ones. No cases in the US.

Sources: CDC: current situation

entry.title: MSF health worker evacuated to the Netherlands
entry.summary: A Medecins Sans Frontieres staff member infected in DR Congo is admitted to Leiden University Medical Center.
entry.content:
A Medecins Sans Frontieres staff member infected in DR Congo is admitted to Leiden University Medical Center.

Sources: ECDC, Cyprus Mail (Reuters)

entry.title: G20 pledges more than US$470 million
entry.summary: New pledges at the G20 foreign ministers' meeting include US$267 million from the US.
entry.content:
New pledges at the G20 foreign ministers' meeting include US$267 million from the US.

Sources: Social News XYZ, Health Policy Watch

entry.title: WHO: 7,890 cases, 3,799 deaths in 63 health zones
entry.summary: The outbreak has reached Dungu health zone, on the border with South Sudan. WHO rates the risk very high in DR Congo and high for neighbouring countries.
entry.content:
The outbreak has reached Dungu health zone, on the border with South Sudan. WHO rates the risk very high in DR Congo and high for neighbouring countries.

Sources: WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON618)

entry.title: Frontline worker vaccine study launched in Bunia
entry.summary: MSF's BRAVO study plans to vaccinate about 20,000 frontline workers in Ituri and North Kivu.
entry.content:
MSF's BRAVO study plans to vaccinate about 20,000 frontline workers in Ituri and North Kivu.

Sources: MSF

entry.title: Outbreak reaches a seventh province, Sud-Ubangi
entry.summary: A death in Bulu health zone marks the first spread to western DR Congo.
entry.content:
A death in Bulu health zone marks the first spread to western DR Congo.

Sources: AP via Local10

entry.title: Vaccination of health workers begins; Uganda declared Ebola-free
entry.summary: DR Congo starts giving Ervebo, a vaccine licensed for a different Ebola species, to health workers in trials. WHO and Africa CDC confirm the end of Uganda's outbreak after 42 days without cases.
entry.content:
DR Congo starts giving Ervebo, a vaccine licensed for a different Ebola species, to health workers in trials. WHO and Africa CDC confirm the end of Uganda's outbreak after 42 days without cases.

Sources: AP via ABC News, WHO Africa

entry.title: WHO keeps the global emergency in place
entry.summary: WHO's Emergency Committee meets for the second time. Modelling it cites suggests true infections may be three to four times the reported count.
entry.content:
WHO's Emergency Committee meets for the second time. Modelling it cites suggests true infections may be three to four times the reported count.

Sources: WHO Emergency Committee report

entry.title: Largest Ebola outbreak in DR Congo's history
entry.summary: With 3,605 confirmed cases in DR Congo, the outbreak passes the 2018–2020 North Kivu outbreak.
entry.content:
With 3,605 confirmed cases in DR Congo, the outbreak passes the 2018–2020 North Kivu outbreak.

Sources: WHO DON614

entry.title: First treatment trial for Bundibugyo Ebola begins
entry.summary: The PARTNERS trial enrols its first patient, testing an antibody treatment and remdesivir.
entry.content:
The PARTNERS trial enrols its first patient, testing an antibody treatment and remdesivir.

Sources: WHO

entry.title: France reports an imported case
entry.summary: An intensive-care doctor returning from DR Congo tests positive in France. He recovers, and none of his contacts fall ill.
entry.content:
An intensive-care doctor returning from DR Congo tests positive in France. He recovers, and none of his contacts fall ill.

Sources: WHO DON612

entry.title: US$518 million response plan launched
entry.summary: Africa CDC and WHO launch a joint continental plan covering June to November 2026.
entry.content:
Africa CDC and WHO launch a joint continental plan covering June to November 2026.

Sources: WHO

entry.title: Africa CDC declares a continental emergency; US restricts entry
entry.summary: Africa CDC declares a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security. The US suspends entry for foreign nationals recently in DR Congo, Uganda or South Sudan.
entry.content:
Africa CDC declares a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security. The US suspends entry for foreign nationals recently in DR Congo, Uganda or South Sudan.

Sources: Africa CDC, STAT

entry.title: WHO declares a global health emergency
entry.summary: The WHO Director-General declares a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, the first time this was done before convening an Emergency Committee.
entry.content:
The WHO Director-General declares a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, the first time this was done before convening an Emergency Committee.

Sources: WHO

entry.title: DR Congo and Uganda declare a Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak
entry.summary: The national lab confirms Bundibugyo virus. It is DR Congo's 17th Ebola outbreak. Uganda confirms a case in Kampala the same day.
entry.content:
The national lab confirms Bundibugyo virus. It is DR Congo's 17th Ebola outbreak. Uganda confirms a case in Kampala the same day.

Sources: WHO DON603, WHO DON602

entry.title: WHO alerted to a deadly unknown illness in Ituri
entry.summary: Reports describe a high-mortality illness in Mongbwalu health zone, including four health workers who died within four days.
entry.content:
Reports describe a high-mortality illness in Mongbwalu health zone, including four health workers who died within four days.

Sources: WHO DON603

entry.title: First known case falls ill in Bunia
entry.summary: A health worker who later died in Bunia, Ituri province, is the earliest known case. Investigators believe the outbreak started in the Mongbwalu mining area.
entry.content:
A health worker who later died in Bunia, Ituri province, is the earliest known case. Investigators believe the outbreak started in the Mongbwalu mining area.
